transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62 mins
Location: Zoom
Recording id: ff-record-20260312-0234
Attendees: Maya (Redwood CSM), Rajiv (Redwood SE), Leo (Redwood Product), Aisha (Lantern Head of ML), Tom (Lantern DevOps), Priya (Lantern Security), Evan (Lantern PM)

Summary: quick alignment on onboarding runway: VPC vs hosted tradeoffs, success criteria for pilot, security checklist (SOC2 + SSO), and next steps for pilot kickoff.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:10 Aisha (Lantern): Hi, Aisha here, head of ML.
00:14 Tom (Lantern): Tom, DevOps.
00:16 Priya (Lantern): Priya, Security.
00:18 Evan (Lantern): Evan, PM.
00:20 Rajiv (Redwood): Rajiv SE here.
00:22 Leo (Redwood): Leo from product.
00:25 Maya (Redwood): Cool. Goal today is to map out a 3-week runway to pilot - confirm constraints, who owns what, and pick model/hosting for initial POC.

02:12 Aisha (Lantern): High-level, we want low latency for chat features in our app, and data not to leave our VPC if possible. Also cost matters — we have a SRE cost target for tokens.
02:28 Maya (Redwood): Totally. We usually recommend starting hosted for speed to value then swap to Dedicated or Private if isolation is required. But if you have strict data egress reqs, Private (VPC) might be better.

05:01 Tom (Lantern): Clarify 'Private' — is that client-managed network or Redwood-managed in VPC? Our legal wants customer-controlled keys.
05:15 Rajiv (Redwood): Private can be VPC-hosted where traffic stays in your cloud. You can bring-your-own-KMS for encryption-at-rest; we have an HSM option for enterprise. sometimes transcription had 'bring-your-own K M S' in notes.
05:40 Priya (Lantern): We need SOC2 Type II evidence and audit logging details. also SAML/SSO for console access.
05:55 Maya (Redwood): We can share SOC2 report, and we support SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning. Audit logs are available per-request in the Console and delivered to your SIEM. We'll attach the security pack.

09:10 Evan (Lantern): On performance, our goal is sub-200ms token latency 95th for short prompts, and about 50 requests/sec peak. Is that realistic?
09:23 Rajiv (Redwood): For typical LLMs, sub-200ms at 95th is aggressive on hosted tier unless we pin to Dedicated GPU pools or use shorter context models and batching tuned. We should run a quick benchmark with your prompt set to be certain.
09:55 Leo (Redwood): Also the model choice matters — smaller dense vs quantized Llama-family variants vs specialized instruction-tuned models. each has different latency and quality tradeoffs.

12:18 Aisha (Lantern): Quality is important, we need hallucination rate under X% — we'll share eval prompts.
12:25 Maya (Redwood): Great, share eval set — we'll run a quality regression and return basic metrics in the pilot.

15:02 Tom (Lantern): What's the suggested network setup for VPC peering? any ip ranges we need to open?
15:12 Rajiv (Redwood): We'll provide a network diagram. Typically you allow outbound to our ingestion endpoint and peer the compute subnets; we also support PrivateLink in AWS. I'll send a template.

18:40 Priya (Lantern): Data retention — do you persist prompts or embeddings? Need to be able to disable retention or have short TTLs.
18:52 Maya (Redwood): For Private deployments you control retention. For hosted, we have options: default short-term retention, and enterprise customers can disable persistence; we'll include config options in the runbook.

23:00 Aisha (Lantern): Our infra runs on GCP — any known issues?
23:08 Rajiv (Redwood): GCP is supported; we have Dedicated pools across major clouds. the main thing is network egress and throughput for streaming. we might recommend a region closer to your users.

27:15 Evan (Lantern): Pricing — we need an estimate for pilot (50k tokens/day) and for projected monthly usage if we go to prod.
27:27 Maya (Redwood): We'll send a pricing worksheet with hosted vs dedicated TCO and estimated per-token costs. For Dedicated we can show reserved capacity vs burst.

31:40 Tom (Lantern): Any constraints on model binaries? we run some internal fine-tune steps; how do we handle custom models?
31:52 Rajiv (Redwood): Private supports bringing your own model artifacts; we have an onboarding flow for model versioning and pinning. For hosted, we can host customer-fine-tuned models under enterprise terms. Some transcription notes: 'fine tune' shown as 'find tine' occasionally.

36:05 Leo (Redwood): Operationally, you'll get Console access with per-route metrics, token breakdowns, and tracing; we'll demo in the pilot. Also we recommend starting with a canary rollout for prod.
36:30 Aisha (Lantern): For success criteria: 1) latency and throughput targets met 2) model quality on eval pass threshold 3) security sign-off from Priya. Anything to add?
36:45 Maya (Redwood): Also: integration completeness (SDKs wired into your backend) and cost within the SRE target.

41:10 Priya (Lantern): Security checklist items — SAML, KMS BYOK, audit logs export, data residency doc. we'll need exact artifact names for legal.
41:28 Maya (Redwood): We'll attach the 'security pack' — SOC2 report, data flow diagrams, certificate for encryption, and the runbook entry for audit logs. Link to placeholder: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (will send actual PDFs).

45:55 Rajiv (Redwood): Pilot plan suggestion: Week 0 — infra prep and network peering; Week 1 — pilot model choice + baseline benchmarks; Week 2 — tuning, canary integration in staging, quality evals; Week 3 — decision checkpoint. we can compress if you want.
46:20 Aisha (Lantern): That timeline looks good. we prefer a fast 2-week loop if possible.
46:30 Maya (Redwood): OK we can accelerate: move bench run to day 2 and tuning day 5. But need contacts and sample prompts quickly.

50:05 Evan (Lantern): Who owns bench infra? do we run load vs you run it?
50:13 Rajiv (Redwood): We can run bench on Redwood infra against your prompt set and provide raw logs; if you want we can share a JMeter/locust job for you to run internally.

53:40 Tom (Lantern): Actionable ask: I'll add the network owner and schedule time with our cloud infra lead.
53:50 Maya (Redwood): Great. we'll also prepare the onboarding repo and share the link: https://redwood.ai/onboard/playbook (placeholder).

57:00 Maya (Redwood): Quick recap before close: Redwood to send onboarding playbook, pricing worksheet, pilot benchmark matrix, and security pack by 2026-03-15. Lantern to send prompt sets, QPS estimates, and VPC peering contact by 2026-03-18. Schedule pilot kickoff (engineering) for week of 2026-03-22.
57:40 Aisha (Lantern): Sounds good.
57:45 Priya (Lantern): I'll review security pack and follow up with a short list.
57:50 Tom (Lantern): I'll share infra diagram and contact.
58:05 Maya (Redwood): Thanks everyone; we'll follow up in email with links and calendar invites.

Closing notes: transcript contains some auto-captions errors (e.g., 'K M S' spacing, 'find-tine' instead of fine-tune). Action items captured above.
